# Tier-1 rewrite pilot — pre-registered decision rule

**Written 2026-08-18, seven days before the data exists.** That is the point: with n=3, an
ambiguous result is trivially easy to read as whatever we already believed. This file fixes
the bar in advance so the 25 August reading is a decision and not a rationalisation.

**Do not edit this file after 2026-08-25.** Record the outcome in a separate section at the
bottom, leaving the criteria untouched.

---

## What is being tested

Three Tier-1 articles were fully regenerated on **2026-07-28**. The 28-day attribution
window closes **2026-08-25**.

| slug | airport | baseline impressions | baseline position |
|---|---|---|---|
| `philadelphia-airport-parking-garage-rates` | PHL | 8,368 | 51.0 |
| `philadelphia-airport-off-site-parking` | PHL | 7,865 | 73.1 |
| `atlanta-airport-extended-parking` | ATL | 7,466 | 37.4 |

All three carry `baselineMetrics` and no `preEdit`, so they will be **measured but never
auto-reverted** (`perf-measure.ts:132` requires `c.preEdit`). The 25 August output is a
reading, not an action.

## Scheduling — this will not happen on its own

The weekly job runs Mondays. On **Mon 24 Aug** these changes are 27 days old and
`perf-measure.ts:110` skips anything younger than the window. The next scheduled run is
**Mon 31 Aug**.

**Someone must run this by hand on 25 August:**

```
node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs src/perf.ts measure --slug philadelphia-airport-parking-garage-rates
node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs src/perf.ts measure --slug philadelphia-airport-off-site-parking
node node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs src/perf.ts measure --slug atlanta-airport-extended-parking
```

## The control groups are sound — verified 2026-08-18

The measurement layer has failed before (empty control cohort for months, then medians so
noisy that 124 changes were wrongly auto-reverted). So the cohorts were inspected in advance
by running `computeControlDelta()` with the real baseline date:

| airport | siblings | median impr move | median pos move | reliable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PHL | 9 | +7.0% | −0.25 | **yes** |
| ATL | 8 | −8.3% | +2.50 | **yes** |

Both draw from `gsc-report-2026-06-28-to-2026-07-26.json`, whose window ends two days before
the edits. Both pass every gate in `perf-control.ts:178-182`. The movements are plausible
seasonality, not the ±200% ramping-cohort artifacts that contaminated the July measurements.

**This removes the main reason to distrust the verdict.** Re-check it on the day — the
cohorts are recomputed at measure time and could drift.

## How `judge()` will decide

From `perf-measure.ts:36-76`, control-adjusted:

- **helped** — impressions up by ≥15% of baseline (≈1,125–1,255 here) **or** position improves by ≥2
- **hurt** — impressions down by that much **or** position worsens by ≥2, with no offsetting gain
- **neutral** — movement inside those bands, or one signal up and one down
- **inconclusive** — baseline too small or no after-data (should not occur; all baselines ≈7,500+)

---

## The pre-registered rule

### What we will conclude

| Outcome | Conclusion | Action |
|---|---|---|
| **3/3 helped** | Rewrites work on deep Tier-1 pages | Second pilot of 25–30, spread across position bands. **Not** a full 1,331 unlock. |
| **2/3 helped, 0 hurt** | Weak positive | Second pilot of 25–30. Same as above — n=3 cannot carry more. |
| **1/3 helped, 0 hurt** | Genuinely inconclusive | Do **not** conclude rewrites fail. Expand the pilot or fix the confound first. |
| **0/3 helped, 0 hurt** | See the confound gate below | Nothing until authority is known. |
| **Any hurt** | Investigate that page individually | Read the diff before drawing any tier-wide conclusion. |

### The confound gate — binding

We have **no backlink data**, and Google weighs inbound links heavily. So a null result has
two incompatible explanations and we currently cannot tell them apart:

- Pilot pages are **link-competitive** with the pages outranking them, and still lost → real
  evidence against rewrites.
- Pilot pages are **link-starved** → the test says nothing about rewriting. A rewrite cannot
  fix an authority deficit.

**Therefore: a 0/3 or 1/3 result may NOT be used to close down Tier-1 rewrites unless we
have link data for the three pages and their top-3 SERP competitors.**

Bing Webmaster was tested on 2026-08-18 as a free source and **returns empty** — site-wide
`GetLinkCounts` gives `Links: [], TotalPages: 0`, and `GetUrlLinks` gives 0 for all three
pilot URLs. A site at ~372k monthly impressions does not plausibly have zero inbound links
site-wide, so this reads as an unpopulated endpoint rather than a true zero. Either way,
**Bing cannot answer this**; a paid source is required.

### What we will NOT conclude, whatever the numbers say

1. **That the result generalises to all 1,331 pages.** Tier-1 median position is 43.5; the
   pilot sits at 37.4 / 51.0 / 73.1 (median 51.0). The spread is fair but the sample is
   three. Any expansion is a bigger pilot, never a full unlock.
2. **That "rewrites don't work" is established by a null result** while the confound gate
   above is open.
3. **That clicks are the success measure.** No Tier-1 page is near page 1 — the best in the
   whole tier is position 21. A successful rewrite here moves a page from 50 to 25 and earns
   almost no clicks. Position and impressions are the honest signals at this depth; clicks
   are not, and we should not be disappointed by their absence.

### Escalation if the result is positive

A second pilot should be **stratified by position band**, not impression-ranked — roughly
8 pages each from 21–35, 36–50, and 51+ — because the rewrite thesis plausibly holds at
position 25 and fails at position 70, and an impression-ranked batch would not separate those.
